system_changes: Tokens, new primitives: font.size.24 (1.5rem), size.20 (1.25rem), size.96 (6rem) and border.width.4 (4px). The descriptions of font.size.28 (now the long total) and size.48 (now also the tab width) are rewritten so they stay true.

Tokens, semantics: font.size.title now aliases font.size.24 (decision 1). New semantics: font.size.display-long (for the 1.75rem long total), size.tab (3rem), size.control-multiline (6rem), size.mark-inset (1.25rem) and border.heavy (4px). The font.size group description now says five sizes.

Tokens, component (decision 2): checkbox.error-edge-width → border.heavy; error-summary.tab-width → size.tab; field.textarea-min-height → size.control-multiline; status.mark-size → size.mark-inset; cost-summary.total-size-long → font.size.display-long.
checkbox.css: the error edge now uses the new error-edge-width token. Before, it borrowed a spacing token as a border width.
field.css: the textarea min-height uses the new token instead of calc(control*2).
status.css: the mark mask size uses the new token instead of calc(mark - space-1).

error-summary.css: the tab width uses the new token. The mark is placed with inset-inline-end: 100% across the tab's width, so the negative calc is gone. The focus ring now shows on :focus (decision 4). Screenshots confirm the mark is still centred.
message.css: its tab is the same 3rem, so it now uses the shared semantic size.tab and drops one calc. Computed values are unchanged.

cost-summary.css: [data-row=total][data-length=long] > dd uses total-size-long. No extra stacking CSS was needed, because the existing flex-wrap already puts the amount below 'Total' at the inline end. Measured at 320 on a panel: the amount spans 51-271px and the display's content box is 49-271px, so it fits in both themes.

base.css, sv-list (decision 6):
- Structure: ul/ol.sv-list of li.sv-list__item. Each item is a flex row that wraps.
- Gaps and lines: a column gap of space-4 and a row gap of space-2, so no focus ring overlaps after a wrap. A divider hairline sits between items.
- Height: min-block-size is the control height when an item holds an a or a button. Items with a trailing button are centred.
- Main part: sv-list__main is a grid with justify-items start. It is never narrower than its longest word.
- Detail lines: sv-list__detail is soft text.
- Trailing part: sv-list__trail sits at the inline end and takes at most 50% of the row. It uses tabular figures and nowrap, and its child elements wrap normally with start alignment.
- How I got there: I tried a 'main keeps half the row' variant. It pushed 'Out of stock' below 'Soap' for no reason, so I reverted it in favour of the 50% cap on the trailing part.

screens.judgment:
I read the screenshots at 320 light, 375 light and dark (checkout-errors), 1280 light (checkout) and 1280 dark (checkout-errors), and the result page at 375 light.

What works:
- Hierarchy and attention: the total is the clearest thing on checkout. It is £60.75 at 36 pixels in the inverse display, against a 24-pixel h1 and 20-pixel h2s, and it is the largest text in every state.
- Pay is the only accent fill in all six states. From the JSON, it is the only control with fill rgb(35,107,207) and the only text on that background. It is 56 pixels tall: 254 wide at 320, 309 at 375 and 446 at 1280.
- Language: every string comes from the shared content or the voice guide. The error summary links and the field error lines match word for word. There are no new marketing words.
- Interaction: the error state is shown by shape as well as colour: the danger mark, ink text at weight 600 and a thick leading edge. On the errors page everything the person typed is kept ('sam.example.com', the name, address and town), and the postcode is empty as typed.
- 1280: the split reads as intended, not as a stretched phone. The form is on the left; the order summary is on the right, top-aligned with Contact, and stays in view. The title, the test notice and the error summary span both columns.
- Dark: the inverse display flips to a light plate and stays distinct, so finding I4 does not come back. No mid-word breaks: 'name@example.com.' wraps whole at 320.

Almost right, reported rather than hidden:
- (1) Pressing Enter in 'Discount code' submits the whole form, which means Pay. That is the browser's implicit submission, and enterkeyhint='done' only labels the key. The system fix is a discount-code pattern in its own form, or a script that turns Enter there into Apply. That is outside 'one form', so it is left for the lead.
- (2) The total row at 320 crosses the 720-pixel line by about 52 pixels (bottom at y=772). The long towel name takes 4 lines.
- (3) The 'Discount code' heading and the field label repeat each other, because the shared content does. I would drop the heading.
- (4) Many panels make a long phone page (2185 pixels at 320). It is consistent with Instrument, but a lighter treatment for the Contact and Discount sections is worth a look.
- (5) The restated 'Total £60.75' above Pay is body size at weight 600. It is quiet, which is right next to a display total, but it is barely more than a label.

inputmode and enterkeyhint are on every text input. The select has autocomplete 'shipping country' only. The checkbox and buttons have neither, because neither attribute applies to them.

screens.judgment:
I looked at these screenshots: assistant at 320 light, 375 light, 375 dark, 1280 light and 1280 dark; assistant-done at 375 light and 1280 dark.

What works:
- Visual hierarchy: three things are plain at a glance on every screenshot.
  - The person's message is an inset plate with a visible edge border, one squared corner and the label 'You'. In dark it stays distinct with colour removed, because the border and the inset remain.
  - The proposal is the one raised panel with a heading.
  - The machine-draft warning has ink text, measured at 13.7:1 in light and 16.52:1 in dark, on a solid amber tab with a triangle mark. Review finding I1 is not repeated.
- Speaker labels: every chat message has a visible label ('Souvenir', 'You', 'Souvenir') in all 12 states. The earlier failed turn carries a 'Souvenir' label too.
- Proposal height at 320 is 629px, under the 720px limit. Heading, fields, draft, warning and primary action all show on one phone screen.
- Accent: the action that commits is 'Move event and send message', because it changes a shared calendar and messages Priya. Sending a message to Souvenir commits nothing, and the screen itself says 'Souvenir has not changed anything yet.' So I made 'Send message' secondary by choosing its variant, with no new CSS. That leaves one accent fill on the screen. On the done screen it is secondary too, so there are no accent fills, on purpose: a control that changes weight between two states of one conversation would break expectation.
- At 1280 the page is a centred 544px reading column, as sv-page gives. After the proposal change the primary sits on one line on its own row, with Edit and Cancel at their own width below. It looks intended, not like a stretched phone.
- Language: I used the shared content's wording exactly, including the longer draft and the full primary label. The brief and the shared file disagreed on the composer button. The brief said 'Send', the shared file says 'Send message', and voice rule 2 allows one-word labels only for Cancel, Close and Done. I used 'Send message'.
- Interaction: the form is method="get" with action="assistant.html". The textarea is labelled 'Message Souvenir'. Edit message and Cancel read as clearly lower ranks than the primary.

Still almost right, left for the lead because it is content, not system:
1. 'Checking both calendars…' keeps turning next to a finished result on both screens, which is close to voice rule 12. I kept it because the brief and the shared content include it. The lead should decide whether a finished turn drops the busy status.
2. 'Try again.' has no control to retry with.
3. At 320 the primary label still wraps to two lines, with its padding kept, as the spec allows.
4. At 320 the suggestion buttons stack one per line, as noted under needs_from_others.

The proposal's h2 heading 'Move the event to Thursday and tell Priya' is my plain-words wording; the shared content gives none.
